_about: One sentence per term, shared by the guided study (hover on a dotted word) and the lab (hover on a panel label, help line under a slider). 'on' lists data-guide names that get this definition as their tooltip; 'help' is the line under a sandbox slider. Physics statements follow docs/PHYSICS.md.

plasma.name: Plasma
plasma.def: A gas hot enough that electrons have left their atoms, so it conducts electricity and can be pushed and held by magnetic fields.

kev.name: keV
kev.def: The temperature unit used in fusion: 1 keV is about 11.6 million °C. A burning D-T plasma needs roughly 10 keV.

dt.name: D-T fusion
dt.def: Deuterium + tritium → helium-4 (3.5 MeV) + a neutron (14.1 MeV): the easiest fusion reaction to reach on Earth.

reactivity.name: Reactivity ⟨σv⟩
reactivity.def: How readily a fuel fuses at a given temperature; for D-T it climbs steeply up to about 65 keV.

tokamak.name: Tokamak
tokamak.def: A doughnut-shaped magnetic bottle that holds a plasma with a strong field around the ring plus the field of a large current driven through the plasma itself.

spherical-tokamak.name: Spherical tokamak
spherical-tokamak.def: A tokamak with a very narrow centre column, shaped like a cored apple; MAST is one. It holds more plasma pressure for a given magnetic field.

q-gain.name: Gain Q
q-gain.def: Fusion power produced divided by heating power put in. Q = 1 is breakeven; ITER's design goal is Q = 10.

tau-e.name: Energy confinement time τ_E
tau-e.def: Stored energy divided by the power leaking out: how long the plasma would take to cool if the heating stopped.

triple-product.name: Triple product n·T·τ_E
triple-product.def: Density × temperature × confinement time; a D-T plasma ignites at roughly 3 × 10²¹ m⁻³·keV·s.

stored-energy.name: Stored energy W
stored-energy.def: The thermal energy held in the plasma, (3/2) ∫ p dV; on MAST it comes from the EFIT reconstruction and includes fast beam ions.

field-line.name: Field line
field-line.def: The path a magnetic field traces; charged particles spiral tightly around field lines, so where the lines go, the plasma goes.

flux-surface.name: Flux surface
flux-surface.def: A closed surface that field lines wind around without leaving it; temperature and density are nearly uniform on each one, so they nest like onion layers.

lcfs.name: Last closed flux surface
lcfs.def: The outermost flux surface that closes on itself: the edge of the confined plasma. Outside it, field lines run into the wall.

x-point.name: X-point
x-point.def: The point where the boundary surface crosses itself, made by the shaping coils; field lines just outside it are led away to the divertor.

sol.name: Scrape-off layer
sol.def: The thin layer just outside the last closed flux surface, where field lines end on the divertor plates and carry the exhaust heat there.

divertor.name: Divertor
divertor.def: The region of the vessel, away from the hot core, where the scrape-off layer's field lines end and the exhaust heat and particles land.

magnetic-axis.name: Magnetic axis
magnetic-axis.def: The centre of the nested flux surfaces, where the plasma is hottest.

safety-factor.name: Safety factor q
safety-factor.def: How many times a field line goes the long way round the ring for each time it goes the short way round; q95 is its value near the edge.

ip.name: Plasma current I_p
ip.def: The current driven through the plasma (about 1 MA on MAST, 15 MA on ITER); it supplies the twist in the field and most of the confinement.
ip.help: The current in the plasma itself. More current confines better and lets the plasma hold more density, but lowers q95 towards the kink limit.

bt.name: Toroidal field B
bt.def: The main magnetic field around the ring, made by external coils; it sets how much current and pressure the plasma can take before going unstable.
bt.help: The main field from the big external magnets. It buys stability (q95 rises with B) and is the most expensive part of the machine.

density.name: Density n
density.def: Electrons per cubic metre, here in units of 10²⁰ m⁻³; on MAST the replay uses the line average from an interferometer.
density.help: How much fuel is in the bottle. Fusion power grows as n², but too much cannot be kept hot, and the Greenwald limit caps it.

heating.name: Heating power
heating.def: Power put into the plasma from outside: ohmic heating by its own current, plus neutral beams or radio waves.
heating.help: External heating. It lights the burn, but confinement gets worse as power goes up (τ<sub>E</sub> ∝ P<sup>−0.69</sup>).

h-factor.name: Confinement multiplier H
h-factor.def: Measured confinement time divided by what a scaling law gives; H98 uses the IPB98(y,2) H-mode law. Above 1 is better than the law.
h-factor.help: Better or worse confinement than the scaling law. Nobody has this knob on a real machine: the Replay tab measures it, and the learned model tries to predict it.

zeff.name: Effective charge Z_eff
zeff.def: A measure of impurities: 1 is pure hydrogen fuel, higher means heavier ions that dilute the fuel and radiate energy away.
zeff.help: How dirty the plasma is. Impurities dilute the fuel and radiate heat away.

nbi.name: Neutral beam injection
nbi.def: Heating by firing fast neutral atoms into the plasma, where they ionise and give their energy to it through collisions.

ohmic.name: Ohmic heating
ohmic.def: Heating by the plasma current flowing through the plasma's own electrical resistance; it fades as the plasma gets hotter and more conductive.

greenwald.name: Greenwald density limit
greenwald.def: An empirical ceiling on density, n_GW = I_p / (π a²): above it the edge cools, the current channel shrinks and the plasma usually disrupts.

beta.name: Beta β, β_N
beta.def: Plasma pressure divided by magnetic pressure. β_N scales it by I_p/(a·B) so machines can be compared.

troyon.name: Troyon limit
troyon.def: The pressure ceiling: above β_N of about 3.5 the plasma pushes hard enough on the field to drive large-scale instabilities.

kink.name: Kink limit
kink.def: With too much current for the field (q95 below about 2) the whole plasma column buckles like an over-twisted rope.

disruption.name: Disruption
disruption.def: A sudden loss of confinement in which the plasma dumps its energy and current onto the vessel within milliseconds.

locked-mode.name: Locked mode
locked-mode.def: A magnetic disturbance that normally rotates with the plasma, stops against the wall and grows; often the step before a disruption.

l-mode.name: L-mode
l-mode.def: Low-confinement mode: the ordinary state of a heated tokamak plasma; the ITER89-P law describes it.

h-mode.name: H-mode
h-mode.def: High-confinement mode: above a power threshold the plasma edge forms a transport barrier and the stored energy roughly doubles.

scaling-law.name: Scaling law
scaling-law.def: A power-law fit of confinement time against current, field, density, power and size across many machines; an empirical summary, not a theory.

ipb98.name: IPB98(y,2)
ipb98.def: The standard H-mode confinement scaling law, fitted to many conventional tokamaks; used to design ITER.

iter89.name: ITER89-P
iter89.def: The standard L-mode confinement scaling law.

efit.name: EFIT
efit.def: The equilibrium reconstruction code: from magnetic measurements outside the plasma it solves for the flux surfaces inside.

magnetics.name: Magnetic diagnostics
magnetics.def: Small pickup coils and flux loops around the vessel that measure the magnetic field and flux; the raw input to EFIT.

thomson.name: Thomson scattering
thomson.def: A laser fired through the plasma: the spread in colour of the light scattered by electrons gives their temperature, its brightness their density.

interferometer.name: Interferometer
interferometer.def: Measures the density averaged along a line through the plasma from how much the plasma delays a laser beam.

pf-coils.name: Poloidal field coils
pf-coils.def: Ring-shaped coils above, below and around the plasma that shape it and hold it in place.

solenoid.name: Central solenoid
solenoid.def: The coil down the centre column that drives the plasma current like a transformer; when its swing runs out the shot must end, which is why tokamak shots are pulses.

surrogate.name: Surrogate model
surrogate.def: A neural network trained to reproduce the output of a slower calculation, or to correct a simple formula, from data.

holdout.name: Holdout test
holdout.def: Judging a learned model only on data it never saw in training; here whole sessions or a whole campaign are kept back, never random shots.

provenance.name: Provenance tags
provenance.def: Every panel says where its content comes from: measured (FAIR-MAST data), model (published laws), learned (PhysicsNeMo), computed (formulas on the measurements).

fair-mast.name: FAIR-MAST
fair-mast.def: UKAEA's open archive of the MAST tokamak's shots (CC BY-SA 4.0); every measured number in this app comes from it.
